title: Saturation: pinch-off and the square law

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Once \(V_{DS}\) reaches the overdrive \(V_{ov} = V_{GS} - V_T\), the gate-to-drain voltage has fallen to exactly \(V_T\), so the inversion layer vanishes at the drain end. This is **pinch-off**. Raising \(V_{DS}\) further does not change the channel: the extra voltage drops across a short high-field region next to the drain, which sweeps arriving electrons into the drain the way a reverse-biased collector junction collects minority carriers.

Because the channel itself still sees \(V_{ov}\) from end to end, the current is the triode expression evaluated at \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\). The channel charge falls linearly from \(C_{ox}V_{ov}\) at the source to zero at pinch-off; its average is half the source value, which is where the factor \(\tfrac12\) comes from. The result is a current set by \(V_{GS}\) and (ideally) independent of \(V_{DS}\): a voltage-controlled current source, which is exactly what an amplifier needs. (Deciding *whether* a device is saturated is the region test from the NMOS-regions skill; here we assume it is.)
sections.figure_alt: Saturation drain current versus gate-source voltage: zero below threshold V_T, then a parabola in the overdrive.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ I_D = \frac12\mu_nC_{ox}\frac WL(V_{GS} - V_T)^2 \]
\[ V_{ov} = \sqrt{\frac{2I_D}{\mu_nC_{ox}W/L}}, \qquad \sqrt{I_D} \propto V_{GS} - V_T \]
At pinch-off \(V_{GD} = V_T\). A plot of \(\sqrt{I_D}\) against \(V_{GS}\) is a straight line crossing the axis at \(V_T\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
Design a device for \(I_D = 180\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) at \(V_{ov} = 0.3\ \mathrm{V}\) with \(\mu_nC_{ox} = 150\ \mu\mathrm{A/V^2}\):
\[ \frac WL = \frac{2(180)}{150(0.09)} \approx 26.7 \]
With \(V_T = 0.45\ \mathrm{V}\), set \(V_{GS} = 0.75\ \mathrm{V}\). Doubling the overdrive to 0.6 V would give four times the current, 720 µA.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Forgetting the \(\tfrac12\), or writing \(I_D \propto V_{GS}^2\) instead of \((V_{GS} - V_T)^2\).
- Thinking current stops at pinch-off. Carriers are swept through the depleted drain region; the current saturates, it does not vanish.
- Confusing MOSFET "saturation" with BJT saturation, which means both junctions forward biased.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Differentiating the square law gives \(g_m = 2I_D/V_{ov}\). The slight upward slope of real saturated curves is channel-length modulation, the subject of the output-resistance skill, and the common-source amplifier is built on this current source.
